transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because my head just hasn’t been working right. It feels foggy, like I’m trying to read through smudged glass or something. At the library I’ll be looking at my old cataloguing notes — and I’ve used those notes for years, you know, the same kind of little marks and reminders — and suddenly I can’t keep my place in them.

And then even deciding the next simple thing, like what to do first, feels… I don’t know, stuck. I’ll sit there staring at it. Funny, I used to be the one people asked where everything belonged, because I had a system for everything. But lately it’s like the system’s there and I’m not quite able to follow it.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I guess… most days it’s been like this for about three months now. It kind of started around when I was getting ready to leave the library — sorting through things, old files and procedures, you know, all the little bits nobody else ever cared about until they needed them. At first I thought it was just that, the change and all, but it hasn’t really lifted.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy during this time?

Yes… yes, I suppose I have. Most days lately I end up just sitting at the kitchen table, and it’s like the color’s gone out of everything. I’ll have my old watercolor books there — I used to like looking through them, the paper and the little notes in the margins, funny how some of those books smell like the old library stacks — but now they just make me feel heavy. Not interested, really. Just… weighed down.
Have you noticed a change in your energy levels or have you been feeling more tired than usual lately?

Yes… tired, but it’s more like everything in my body has been slowed down. Like walking to the corner store — and it’s not far, I’ve walked it for years, same cracked bit of sidewalk by Mrs. Keller’s old place — it feels like I’m dragging myself there.

Even at my desk, just sorting papers into piles, which used to be nothing for me, takes more effort than it should. I’ll pick up one sheet and then just sit there a minute before the next one. It’s embarrassing, really.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or sometimes feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Yes… slower, mostly. I don’t think I’m pacing around or anything like that. It’s more like my body’s gotten stuck in thick syrup, if that makes sense.

Even walking to the corner store feels like such a production now, and it’s just down the way — I used to pop over there without thinking. And papers on my desk, sorting them into stacks… that used to be automatic for me at the library. Now I’ll just sit there holding one page longer than I should, like I’m waiting for my hands to remember what comes next.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently? Like eating less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Yes… eating less, I think. I don’t always notice it right away, but I have to sort of remind myself, like, “You should eat something now.” My wife notices more than I do. She’ll look at my bowl and say I’ve left half the rice, or the soup’s gone cold and I’ve barely touched it.

Which is odd for me, because I was raised not to waste food — my mother was very strict about that, you know, even a spoonful left behind was a whole lecture. So it bothers me a little, seeing food still there. Before, I would’ve finished a meal without thinking. Now I just… stop halfway.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or that life isn’t worth living?

I… I don’t think so. Not like making a plan or wanting to hurt myself, if that’s what you mean.

Sometimes when you sit too long with your own thoughts, they get a bit… crowded, I suppose. My father used to say idle time was bad for a man, though he also fell asleep in his chair every evening after the news, so I don’t know. But no, I haven’t been thinking about doing something to myself. It’s more just… trying to get through the day, I guess.
Have you ever felt this way before, with similar feelings of sadness and low energy, or is this the first time you’ve experienced something like this?

I’m… not really sure how to answer that. I mean, everyone has rough patches, don’t they? There were times years ago when work felt heavy, especially when the library changed its filing system — people think shelving and paperwork are simple, but if the labels are wrong, the whole thing becomes a mess.

But feeling like this exactly? I don’t know. I can’t quite say. My memory for those things isn’t very neat… it’s not like keeping old receipts in a box where you can sort by year. So I’m not sure if this is the first time or just the first time I’ve really noticed it this much.
Has this low mood and difficulty with daily tasks been going on for more than two years?

More than two years? No… I don’t think it’s been that long.

It’s more like… maybe three months? Around when I started getting ready to leave the library. Funny, you spend years knowing where everything goes — forms in one drawer, stamps in another — and then when you have to pack up your own things, suddenly even a pencil cup feels like a big decision.

But yes, the low mood, the foggy feeling, finding daily things harder… that’s been most days for about three months, not years.
